questions.stem: He is (A)/ one of the tallest (B)/ boy in the class. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'One of the' is always followed by a plural noun. 'boy' should be 'boys'. Correct: 'He is one of the tallest boys in the class.'

questions.stem: She insisted (A)/ on me going (B)/ to the party. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: B is correct. A gerund after a preposition must be preceded by a possessive pronoun. 'me going' should be 'my going'. Correct: 'She insisted on my going to the party.'

questions.stem: Neither of the (A)/ two candidates (B)/ have secured full marks. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Neither of' takes a singular verb. 'have' should be 'has'. Correct: 'Neither of the two candidates has secured full marks.'

questions.stem: Between you and I, (A)/ the plan seemed (B)/ unlikely to succeed. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: A is correct. After a preposition ('between'), the object form must be used. 'I' should be 'me'. Correct: 'Between you and me, the plan seemed unlikely to succeed.'

questions.stem: The police have (A)/ arrested three persons (B)/ suspected of robbery. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Police' is a collective noun that takes a plural verb ('have') in standard British/Indian English. The sentence is grammatically correct as written.

questions.stem: The teacher (A)/ as well as the students were (B)/ present at the gathering. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: B is correct. When 'as well as' joins two subjects, the verb agrees with the first subject ('teacher' = singular). 'were' should be 'was'. Correct: 'The teacher as well as the students was present...'

questions.stem: He has been working (A)/ in this company (B)/ since ten years. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Since' is used with a point in time (since 2014). For a span/duration, use 'for'. Correct: 'He has been working in this company for ten years.'

questions.stem: I had went (A)/ to the market (B)/ before she called. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Had' requires the past participle form. 'went' is simple past; the past participle of 'go' is 'gone'. Correct: 'I had gone to the market before she called.'

questions.stem: Ramesh is one of (A)/ those brilliant students who has (B)/ won many prizes. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: B is correct. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'those brilliant students' (plural), so the verb must be plural. 'has' should be 'have'. Correct: '…those brilliant students who have won many prizes.'

questions.stem: Scarcely had she (A)/ reached the station (B)/ than the train left. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: C is correct. The correlative construction with 'Scarcely' uses 'when', not 'than'. ('No sooner...than' is correct, but 'Scarcely/Hardly...when'.) 'than' should be 'when'. Correct: 'Scarcely had she reached the station when the train left.'
